summary: Bizarre Creations' Kudos-based street-racing lineage, from Metropolis Street Racer through the Xbox and Xbox 360 Project Gotham Racing games and mobile spin-offs.

entries.title: Metropolis Street Racer

emulation.notes: Use VGA output or high-resolution Dreamcast emulation.

primary.why: Metropolis Street Racer is a Dreamcast-exclusive predecessor to Project Gotham Racing, with the Kudos system, London/Tokyo/San Francisco city routes, time-of-day behavior, and 262 tracks. The final PAL and US discs avoid the major launch bugs and are the complete route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the final PAL or US Dreamcast disc on Dreamcast hardware with VGA output or via Flycast/Redream.

entries.remaster_caveats: The planned Japanese release was canceled; early PAL discs had major bugs and should not be the preferred route.

entries.title: Project Gotham Racing

emulation.notes: Use original hardware or verify emulator compatibility.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Xbox output or emulator scaling

primary.why: The first Project Gotham Racing was released exclusively for Xbox as a launch title, retaining MSR's Kudos concept while moving to four cities and 204 circuits. There is no sourced enhanced or remastered release, so the original Xbox version is definitive.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original Xbox hardware or a compatible Xbox emulator such as xemu; use widescreen/progressive output where supported by the setup.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern remaster or backward-compatible digital route is sourced.

entries.title: Project Gotham Racing 2
entries.definitive_edition: Original Xbox release plus Paris and Long Beach Booster Packs

emulation.notes: Use DLC-capable preservation setup for the complete route; Insignia can restore some online functions where supported.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Original Xbox output or emulator scaling

primary.version: Original Xbox release with Paris and Long Beach DLC if preserved
primary.why: Project Gotham Racing 2 is an Xbox-exclusive sequel with expanded cities, cars, Xbox Live support, and two DLC packs adding Paris/Long Beach tracks and cars. The complete route is the original Xbox version with both DLC packs preserved.
primary.how_to_play: Play on original Xbox hardware or xemu; install the Paris Booster Pack and Long Beach Booster Pack if a legitimate preserved DLC setup is available.

entries.remaster_caveats: Original Xbox Live service ended; online play now depends on replacement-service preservation, and DLC access depends on preserved entitlement/setup.

entries.title: Project Gotham Racing 3
entries.definitive_edition: Xbox 360 release plus Cadillac/Speed/Style DLC where preserved

emulation.notes: Use original hardware for best reliability; verify Xenia status before relying on emulation.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Xbox 360 HD output or emulator scaling

primary.version: Xbox 360 release with DLC if preserved
primary.why: Project Gotham Racing 3 is an Xbox 360 launch-window exclusive focused on high-detail supercars, cockpit view, Xbox Live play, and DLC packs. The only complete route is the Xbox 360 release with the Cadillac, Speed, and Style content preserved where available.
primary.how_to_play: Play on Xbox 360 hardware with installed DLC if owned/preserved, or test compatibility in Xenia.

entries.remaster_caveats: No sourced remaster or modern purchase route; DLC availability may be preservation-dependent.

entries.title: Project Gotham Racing 4

emulation.notes: Original hardware is the reliable route; use Xenia only after checking current compatibility.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Xbox 360 HD output or emulator scaling

primary.why: Project Gotham Racing 4 is the final mainline entry, exclusive to Xbox 360, adding weather systems, Bulldog mode, motorcycles, expanded cities/tracks, and more than 130 vehicles. It is the only and complete platform route.
primary.how_to_play: Play the Xbox 360 disc on Xbox 360 hardware, or test compatibility in Xenia for higher-resolution preservation.

entries.remaster_caveats: Online-era features depend on surviving Xbox Live support/state; no modern remaster is sourced.

entries.title: Project Gotham Racing Mobile

emulation.notes: Use original handsets or specialized mobile emulation where possible.

primary.why: Project Gotham Racing Mobile began as a J2ME mobile-phone release and was followed by a 2007 smartphone version for Symbian and Windows Mobile. The smartphone version is the best-fidelity mobile route where preserved.
primary.how_to_play: Use preserved Symbian/Windows Mobile hardware or emulator setups; keep the J2ME version only as an earlier mobile variant.

entries.remaster_caveats: Mobile preservation depends on handset/OS/emulator availability.

entries.title: Project Gotham Racing: Ferrari Edition

emulation.notes: Use original Zune HD hardware/software where available.

primary.why: Ferrari Edition is a Zune HD-exclusive spin-off focused on Ferrari, released in 2009 as the last Project Gotham Racing-branded game. Zune HD is the sole platform.
primary.how_to_play: Play on preserved Zune HD hardware/software if available.

entries.remaster_caveats: No modern rerelease is sourced; hardware preservation is required.
